gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured discharge figure for any 500 Wh LiFePO4 candidate. Named tests put them close together: StorageReview's 512 Wh-rated EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max delivered 410 Wh before shutting off, and APH Networks drew 403.9 Wh at 134 W from the 448 Wh-rated BLUETTI AC50B, which is 90.2% of its rating against about 80% for the EcoFlow.
standout_why: I opened both cited rival pages. Powerbencher's 500 Wh roundup (published 2026-07-31) says it used 0 units hands-on and only applies a 15% loss assumption to maker capacity. The powerstations.reviews database says it is built 'on the maker's own figures' and shows no tested Wh, efficiency, idle draw or noise. The cited HSN EcoFlow PDF is an image with no readable text. ChatGPT's line '400–450Wh of usable AC energy' is a generic estimate with no tester behind it. I did not open the uncited results (stationarena, offgridpick, sunergyhub, wattandwarden and the rest), so one of them may hold a measurement.
decides: This backs EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max 500 as best overall value but does not settle the pick. Measured output for the RIVER 2 Max (410 Wh) and the AC50B (404 Wh) is nearly the same, so the AC50B's lower 448 Wh rating costs only about 6 Wh in practice. The RIVER 2 Max also recharged from 2% to 100% in just under 1 hour in StorageReview's test, which matches its main selling point. I found no named measurement for the Jackery Explorer 500 v2, the BLUETTI AC50P or the Anker SOLIX 536, so the '6,000 cycles' and '700 W' picks still rest only on maker specs. One caveat: StorageReview tested the original 512 Wh RIVER 2 Max, and EcoFlow's US store now sells the 'RIVER 2 Max 500' rated at 499 Wh.

findings.label: Energy delivered before shutdown (StorageReview, Jordan Ranous)
findings.note: Remote-lab discharge run until the unit powered off. Load wattage is not stated. 410 ÷ 512 = 80.1% of rated capacity. This is the original 512 Wh unit, while the current US listing is the 499 Wh 'RIVER 2 Max 500', so 410 ÷ 499 = 82.2% holds only if the hardware is the same, which I did not confirm.
